title: One line, and the strands of the same surname that no record joins to it
caption: Where each of these Falco came from and where each of them went: one line, and the strands of the same surname that no record joins to it

lanes.label: Out of Arienzo, by marriage

nodes.why: The earliest document of the line: Pasquale's baptism, 24 July 1767, names his father Matteo. Seven generations, most of them on one street — strada Camellara.
Generation eight was born here because generation seven married an Annecchino of Forchia. A marriage moved a family that had not moved in seven generations.
Where Carmine Falco married Francesca Zampiello, on 15 January 1955 — her home town.
The ss SYDNEY of the Lauro Lines, Genoa to Brisbane, arrived 26 March 1964.

ends: Five Falco graves in the Catholic cemetery at Nudgee, Brisbane.
lanes.statusNote: origin not found · Paolisi 1714 is a candidate, not joined

lanes.label: Out of Paolisi, into Arienzo
nodes: «infanti nato ex FRANCISCO FALCO CASALIS PAULISII» — the baptism states his origin outright. It is the earliest Arienzo Falco household with a stated place of origin.
Giuseppe, baptised at Sant'Andrea in July 1714.
A son whose given name will not read as either Matteo or Martino.
Domenico, baptised February 1726 — the last of them.
ends: Twelve years before Matteo's generation, and nothing whatever joins it to this line. It would be a satisfying answer to where the family came from, which is exactly why it is drawn apart.

lanes.label: The Falco of San Felice a Cancello
nodes: «ho battezzato la figlia di TOMASO FALCO e MARTA MARA coniugi … e li ho imposto nome LUCRETIA» — written in Italian, not Latin. The earliest Falco entry this archive holds anywhere.
SEBASTIANO FALCO and his son LUIGI, eighteen, both SAPUNARO — soap-makers — of strada Croce di San Felice, with COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO, fifty-five, filatrice.
Luigi Falco marries at Arienzo as a minor, assisted by both parents. It is the only crossing between the two towns in the Falco name.
ends: Generation four's wife was born at San Felice a Cancello three years later, on 24 February 1818, at the Massaria delle Fosse. THE SAME TOWN IS NOT A CONNECTION. Nothing joins the soap-makers to her or to this line.

lanes.label: The gentry Falco of Arienzo
nodes: DON FRANCESCO FALCO, PROPRIETARIO, and DONNA MADDALENA SICILIANO — her name read from the image on 20 September 2026 and new to this archive.
«è morta nel Monastero d'AVE GRATIA PLENA, DONNA RAFFAELA DE' FALCO, d'anni SESSANTASETTE … di professione MONACA, figlia di DON FRANCESCO FALCO Defunto, di professione PROPRIETARIO».
ends: a nun d. 1850 and a priest d. 1857?

A landowner and his daughter, a nun dead at sixty-seven. The archive also holds a Don Francesco Falco whose wife is written Donna Maddalena Stellato, with a daughter, a nun, dead 14 November 1850, and a son, a priest, dead 20 June 1857; it keeps both wives' names under one household and has not reconciled them. Ours are contadini and braccianti. Plainly a different household living elsewhere in the same town.

lanes.label: The Falco of the valle Caudina

nodes.why: Four hundred and six Falco harvested from the Paolisi registers. All of them reach the register and the search index; not one of them is claimed as kin.
Three hundred and ten more. Deciding whether any of these belongs to this family is a reading job on 716 rows that has never been started.

ends: Giving them a household would be a claim, not a promotion. They are searchable and they are unjoined, and that is the honest state of them.

bridges.label: candidate origin of the line — no record joins them

pens.note: Documented, dated households of the name in the same parish, each placed to a street or a house number. No record joins any of them to the line or to each other; a shared surname in one small town is suggestive and is not evidence. What would move one onto a lane is an act that names a parent, a spouse or a kinsman on it.
items: A second Michelangelo, a Michele, a Francesco and an older Michele, on the same short street as the line. Nothing in any register joins them to the line or to each other. A shared surname in one small town is suggestive and is not evidence.
At numbers 2 and 9, 3, 4, 8, 10 and 14, each documented, dated and placed to a house number. Numbers 8 and 10 also hold a death of this line. No act joins any of the six to the line or to each other.

Numbers 57, 70, 77, 80, 82, 83, 88 and 89: a second cluster of the name, in a different quarter from strada Camellara. Three of them are proved brothers by their own marriage acts; nothing read attaches any of them to this line.
Strada Costa — Giuseppe Falco and Gelsomina Vigliotta

The other Giuseppe Falco, not the Giuseppe of strada Camellara, of the parish of Santa Maria ad Nives. Their son Domenico married Mariantonia Frasca at Santa Maria a Vico in 1844. No kinship to the line is claimed.

pens.note: Falco of other parishes, recorded so that nobody joins them to the line by mistake. Falco is a common Campanian name, and no kinship to the line is claimed or suspected.
items: Antonio Falco and Vincenza della Zorca, coloni, living with their daughter at Santa Maria a Vico in 1872. Not the Antonio Falco this archive already holds, who married Carmela Guida. No kinship to the line is claimed.

Francesco Falco, born at Airola, son of the late Pietro Falco and Camilla Carbone, who married at Arienzo in 1848. He is recorded so that nobody joins him by mistake; no kinship is claimed or suspected.
A proprietario born at Naples about 1818 and living at Arienzo in 1884, when he married at Santa Maria a Vico.
